description: Single-panel scatter/regression-style plot quantifying how aluminium additions lighten Fe-Mn-Al-C austenitic steels. The abscissa is "Aluminium content [wt.%]" (0–14, ticks every 2). There is a dual ordinate: the left axis is "mass density [g/cm³]" (6.50–8.00, ticks every 0.25) and the right axis is "density reduction [%]" (0 at top to 18 at bottom, i.e. inverted so that going down means more reduction). Data markers are open symbols on a white-to-grey vertical gradient background. A single open square sits at about 0 wt.% Al with the printed legend "regime of conventional steels, 7.874 g/cm³"; one open circle near 3 wt.% Al is labelled "conventional TRIP/TWIP-steels"; a series of teal open squares runs from roughly 6 to 13 wt.% Al, with mass density falling steadily from about the 7.15 to the 6.4 level as Al rises, reaching close to the 18% density-reduction tick at the highest Al content. Text annotations cluster the squares: "<18 %Mn", "18-26 %Mn" and "26-30 %Mn" beside successive groups, and green region labels "TRIPLEX-steels", "low density TWIP steels" and "low density duplex steels". No numeric values are printed on the individual data points; only axis ticks, the 7.874 g/cm³ label and the annotation strings are readable.

observations.observation: The x-axis is labelled 'Aluminium content [wt.%]' and runs from 0 to 14 with ticks every 2.
The left ordinate is labelled 'mass density [g/cm³]' spanning 6.50 to 8.00 with ticks every 0.25.
The right ordinate is labelled 'density reduction [%]', printed with 0 at the top and 18 at the bottom, i.e. an inverted scale.
An open square at about 0 wt.% Al carries the printed text 'regime of conventional steels, 7.874 g/cm³'.
An open circle near 3 wt.% Al at a mass density between the 7.25 and 7.50 gridlines is labelled 'conventional TRIP/TWIP-steels'.
Teal open squares are annotated in three Mn-bracketing groups printed as '<18 %Mn', '18-26 %Mn' and '26-30 %Mn'.
Three region labels are printed in the upper right area: 'TRIPLEX-steels', 'low density TWIP steels' and 'low density duplex steels'.
Moving right along the plot, mass density decreases monotonically with rising Al content; the rightmost squares sit just above the 6.50 gridline, close to the 18% density-reduction tick.
No numeric values are printed next to individual data points; only the 7.874 g/cm³ reference label and axis ticks give quantitative anchors.
The caption states the figure shows density reduction in Fe-Mn-Al-C TWIP steels as a function of Al content.
The citing text asserts that this alloy concept enables density reductions of up to 18% (Fig. 1).
The citing text notes that some of the data shown here stem from the work of Georg Frommeyer.

subfigures.description: Scatter plot of mass density (left axis, g/cm³) and density reduction (right axis, %, inverted) versus Aluminium content (x axis, wt.%), with one conventional-steel reference square at ~0 wt.% Al labelled 'regime of conventional steels, 7.874 g/cm³', one open circle labelled 'conventional TRIP/TWIP-steels', and a descending series of teal open squares from ~6 to ~13 wt.% Al annotated '<18 %Mn', '18-26 %Mn', '26-30 %Mn' and region-labelled 'TRIPLEX-steels', 'low density TWIP steels', 'low density duplex steels'.
